title: Problem Overview
content:
**Erdős Problem #311** (Erdős–Graham 1980, OPEN):

Define δ(N) = min{|1 − Σ_{n∈A} 1/n| : A ⊆ {1,...,N}, Σ ≠ 1, Σ ≤ 1} — the minimal nonzero deviation from 1 achievable by unit fraction sums.

**Conjecture:** δ(N) = e^{−(c+o(1))N} for some constant c ∈ (0,1).

**Known:** e^{−(1+o(1))N} ≤ δ(N) ≤ exp(−cN/(log N · log log N)³).
mathContext: This problem connects number theory (lcm estimates via PNT), subset-sum problems, and exponential decay rates. Kovac showed the subset-sum-to-1 variant is equivalent.

title: Unit Fraction Sum and δ(N)
content:
**unitFracSum A:** computes Σ_{n∈A} 1/n for a finite set A ⊆ ℕ.

**delta N = δ(N):** axiomatised as the minimal nonzero value of |1 − unitFracSum A| over subsets A ⊆ {1,...,N} with sum ≤ 1 and sum ≠ 1.

**delta_pos:** δ(N) > 0 for N ≥ 1 — the minimum is achieved and is strictly positive.

δ(N) captures how closely 1 can be approximated (but not reached) by sums of distinct unit fractions from {1,...,N}.
mathContext: The function δ(N) is well-defined by finiteness of subsets. It measures a form of 'Diophantine approximation' using unit fractions rather than rationals.

title: Lower Bound via lcm
content:
**delta_lower_bound:**

δ(N) ≥ e^{−(1+ε)N} for large N.

**Proof idea:** Any nonzero deviation |1 − Σ 1/n| is at least 1/lcm(1,...,N), since clearing denominators gives an integer. By the Prime Number Theorem, lcm(1,...,N) = e^{(1+o(1))N} (Chebyshev's formula).

So δ(N) ≥ e^{−(1+o(1))N}, giving exponential decay with rate 1.
mathContext: The lcm lower bound is the 'trivial' bound. The conjecture asks whether the true rate c is strictly less than 1 — meaning δ(N) decays slower than 1/lcm.

title: Tang's Upper Bound
content:
**tang_upper_bound:**

δ(N) ≤ exp(−cN/(log N · log log N)³) for some c > 0.

This is subexponential: faster than any polynomial decay, but much slower than the conjectured e^{−cN}. The triple logarithmic factor (log N · log log N)³ in the denominator significantly weakens the exponential rate.

Tang's result uses sophisticated constructions of near-1 unit fraction sums.
mathContext: The gap between Tang's subexponential upper bound and the conjectured exponential rate e^{−cN} is enormous. Closing this gap is the central challenge.

title: The Erdős–Graham Conjecture (OPEN)
content:
**erdos_311_conjecture:**

There exists c ∈ (0,1) such that δ(N) = e^{−(c+o(1))N}.

Formally: for every ε > 0 and large N:
e^{−(c+ε)N} ≤ δ(N) ≤ e^{−(c−ε)N}

This says δ(N) decays at a precise exponential rate c strictly between 0 and 1.

**Why c < 1?** Because c = 1 would mean δ ~ 1/lcm, which is the trivial lower bound.
**Why c > 0?** Because δ(N) > 0 (you can't exactly reach 1 for most N).
mathContext: The conjecture predicts that the best unit fraction approximation to 1 decays exponentially with a well-defined rate. This would be a deep result about the structure of Egyptian fraction decompositions.
